manual_package.common_premise: Fixed R with valid native Tone/Color and numeric inputs unless noted. GameStats.play_time is a stateful getter: if GameTemp last-uptime anchor exists, add System.uptime minus anchor to stored play_time and refresh anchor; otherwise return stored value. Every consumer below can therefore update saved Stats. No native/game execution or frame/visible-output assurance. Durations are converted from1/20seconds, not current Graphics frame count.

Nonzero path clones initial/target, converts duration/20.0, then stores mutable play_time getter result as start. facts.meaning: Picture.update returns when nameempty, otherwise takes one mutable play_time snapshot for movement/tone. Rotation separately uses System.uptime: rotate(nonzero) captures uptime, zero sets timer nil; update initializes missing timer, adds speed*(uptime-timer)*20, refreshes timer, wraps angle to0..360. Thus rotation and movement/tone are different clock domains. Loaded/nonfresh timer state is not rebased by this body unless nil.
facts.control: speed0 skips rotation regardless of old timer; no global pause/load compatibility promise follows. Multiple picture updates can read different play_time values in one outer call, unlike Screen's commonnow for its own effects.
facts.failure_prefix: Stats and earlier movement/tone fields can be committed before rotation failure. Native uptime is read multiple times, not an atomic single sample. No rollback.
facts.open: Cross-session uptime behavior/old save shapes, global update scheduling and native execution are not tested or newly specified; whole relevant formal owner/history must be read before any new finding.

def lerp(start_val, end_val, duration, delta, now = nil)
  return end_val if duration <= 0
  delta = now - delta if now
  return start_val if delta <= 0
  return end_val if delta >= duration
  return start_val + ((end_val - start_val) * delta / duration.to_f)
end

def play_time
    if $game_temp&.last_uptime_refreshed_play_time
      now = System.uptime
      @play_time += now - $game_temp.last_uptime_refreshed_play_time
      $game_temp.last_uptime_refreshed_play_time = now
    end
    return @play_time
  end
